title: Neurological and metabolic related pathophysiologies and treatment of comorbid diabetes with depression.
authors: Li S, Yang D, Zhou X, Chen L, Liu L, Lin R, Li X, Liu Y, Qiu H, Cao H, Liu J, Cheng Q.
figures: The pathogenesis underlying the comorbidity between diabetes mellitus and depression. HPA, Hypothalamic–Pituitary–Adrenal; GM, Gastrointestinal Microbiome. By Figdraw.

The neurological system, including brain structure and function, neurogenesis, BDNF, and neurotransmitter, are involved in the pathophysiology of diabetes mellitus and depression. APDs, Antipsychotic drugs; DA, Dopamine; NE, Norepinephrine. NSC, Neuron stem cell; SSRIs, Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors; By Figdraw.

Obesity may lead to diabetes mellitus and depression through reduced adiponectin and increased leptin and resistin. Leptin increased the expression of PPARγ to up‐regulate the activation phenotype of microglia, and related to insulin resistance.
